note: Every capture here is SYNTHETIC. These cases exercise the analyzer; they say nothing about any device. Expected files are worked out by hand (and cross-checked by tests/e02/oracle.py), never produced by the analyzer. Each expected file is a SUBSET of the report: named keys must match exactly, arrays must match in length and element by element.

cases.title: clean capture: full coverage, dropouts known to be zero, absolute verdict without any baseline
five underruns, one per evidence class: source outage, network lateness, CPU deadline miss, output underrun, ambiguous
underrun with no discriminating signals in the capture: undetermined, missing signals named
no underrun counter and no device clock: dropout count is unknown, not zero, and a zero-dropout threshold is not met
coverage hole with events inside it: reported, never interpolated, events unlocated
capture ends before its declared duration: truncation reported, no extrapolation
32-bit wraparound counted exactly; 32-bit and 64-bit resets censored, never a negative rate
wall clock steps forward and back: reported, no fake gap or dropout, real dropout still found
implausible reading rejected, spike kept and flagged, percentiles by nearest rank
device sample clock: drift against monotonic time, 32-bit wrap is not a stall, a real stall is found
out-of-order and duplicate timestamps rejected and counted, never re-ordered
two snapshots: a shared page counted once (PSS), naive RSS double count reported, kernel memory kept apart, peak and headroom
contradictory /proc inputs are reported as findings and nothing is silently corrected
16 KiB pages: statm page counts convert through the explicit page size; absent fields stay absent
comparative claim without a baseline is refused
a synthetic capture cannot serve as the incumbent baseline
a margin of 100% or more is refused rather than clamped
wrong capture schema version is refused at line 1
a sample naming an undeclared series is refused
a non-integer timestamp is refused
a /proc value with the wrong unit is refused, not guessed
unknown subcommand prints usage and exits 2
a series capture exactly as the human-run recipe's sampler writes it (generic profile, mono_ns from uptime, whole-second wall_ns, thresholds declared first) is accepted and analyzed as hand-computed
a memory file exactly as the recipe's snapshot script writes it (header, label, uptime-derived time, raw meminfo/status/smaps_rollup/statm sections) is accepted and accounted as hand-computed
an address, a MAC, a serial and a host name that appear only in # comments are never copied into the report
a profile that is an address is refused by field and class, and the address is not echoed
a series named by a serial-looking string is refused by field and class, and the serial is not echoed
a snapshot labelled by a MAC address is refused by field and class, and the MAC is not echoed
a process name shaped like a serial is replaced in the memory report by <redacted:serial>, an ordinary name next to it is kept, and a comment's address is not copied
an unknown first token that is an address is reported as <redacted:ipv4>, never repeated
a sixty-character unknown token is repeated in a diagnostic as at most thirty-two characters
a line longer than the 4096-byte limit, even a comment, is refused before anything is read from it
a qualified series reads plainly on stderr: verdict, evidence, coverage as exact integers, holes, truncation, dropouts, causes, findings; stdout stays exactly one line of JSON

invariants.text: kB/KiB/page conversions use an explicit page size; a wrong unit is an error
a shared page is counted once (PSS); the naive RSS overstatement is reported
kernel buffers and driver residual are accounted separately from process RSS
peak and steady memory both reported; headroom judged only against a reserve declared in the input
a field the kernel does not provide stays absent, never zero
coverage and sample denominators are exact integers
gaps are coverage holes; events inside them are unlocated, never spread
a capture that ends early reports what is missing and does not extrapolate
a falling monotonic counter is a reset, never a negative rate
a physically possible 32-bit wraparound is counted exactly
a wall-clock step creates no gap and no dropout
the device sample clock is related to monotonic time by drift, not mixed with it
source outage, network lateness, CPU deadline miss and output underrun are told apart by their own signals
without the discriminating signal the cause is undetermined and the missing signal is named
no dropout signal in the capture means unknown, never zero
implausible readings are excluded and counted; spikes are kept and flagged
absolute results and declared-threshold verdicts work with no comparison baseline
a comparative claim without a measured baseline is refused, by type
malformed or ambiguous input is rejected with a typed, bounded, line-numbered error
a capture written exactly as the human-run recipe's scripts write one is accepted, and the report matches a hand-computed expectation, so the recipe and the parser agree
a profile, series name or snapshot label with the shape of an address, MAC, serial or host name is refused by line, field and class, and the text is not echoed
comment lines are never copied into a report, so identifiers in a comment cannot leave through it
a process name copied from /proc is redacted when it has an identifier's shape, and an ordinary name is kept
input text repeated in a diagnostic is redacted to its class when it has an identifier's shape
every result is one line of JSON that names its schema version, its evidence class and, for a series, its profile, and says it was not measured on a device
the report exposes how many findings were dropped at the cap, so a bounded list is never silently short

output is bounded: a line over 4096 bytes is refused, and input text repeated in a diagnostic is cut to 32 characters (the cap of 256 findings per report is a Rust unit test, findings_are_capped_and_the_overflow_is_counted)

evidence the capture lost is reported as lost, never as a complete clean result: a truncated capture, a coverage hole, a missing signal and an undetermined cause each say so and leave the verdict unmet or not assessed

after the JSON report, each run that writes one prints exactly one concise human line on stderr and stdout stays exactly one line of JSON; the line is derived only from the report's own fields, shows the verdict or claim, coverage as its exact integers, dropouts and causes, reads unknown and undetermined as exactly that (never as zero or none), and reads a refused comparison as refused; a run that wrote no report prints no summary

no input text leaves through the summary line: it carries numbers and the analyzer's fixed words only, so a profile, series name, snapshot label, process name or comment holding a site identifier cannot appear in it

invariants.inapplicable: Run, case and correlation IDs, event timestamps, member and group IDs, source epoch, command and state revision, queue and latency counters, the injected fault schedule and a causal error chain describe a running system that emits events. The analyzer is a batch function over one file with no members, sessions, commands or fault injection: a result is identified by its case ID, the input file and the profile and evidence the report names, and a refusal is a typed error with its line number.

There is no render path, no log sink and no audio payload in this crate: it reads text files, never the audio they describe, and the capture format has no field that could carry samples. The clause that slow, full or unavailable sinks must not change an audio deadline therefore has nothing to apply to here; it belongs to the render-path tasks.

invariants.text: Failure output retains per-case replay, artifact digests, versions and observed profile when the case is identifiable; global/orphan checks retain their applicable artifacts and explicit unavailable context. The named planted test functions, not ordinary clean analyzer cases, exercise retention. The local oracle's owned group is cleaned up on timeout/signal; the remote Rust half is bounded only by RCH's own deadline. No retry is implemented (a design fact, not a separately tested guarantee).

invariants.inapplicable: The analyzer is a pure batch function over a file: it has no long-running work to cancel and no state to restart from, and it writes its single report only after the whole input has been analyzed, so there is no partial-report state. A killed run produces no output.

No incumbent resource or dropout capture exists in either repository and this task has no authority over a live device. Measuring the incumbent is a separate externally authorised receipt that this analyzer would consume; nothing here claims it.
